checkpoints.title: Tradeoff duel
checkpoints.prompt: 500M DAU, ~100M posts/day, and a feed must load fast.

options.label: Assemble the feed on read
options.verdict: Fresh, and it puts a fan-in query on the most frequent operation in the product. For a read-heavy social graph that is the wrong side of the trade.

options.label: Precompute timelines on write
options.sub: push post ids to follower feeds
options.verdict: Reads become a single list fetch. You pay once per post rather than once per feed view, which at 500M DAU against 100M posts is overwhelmingly the cheaper side.

defend.prompt: What does precomputing timelines force on you?

options.label: Celebrity accounts need a pull-based exception
Timelines are built for users who never open the app
Feed storage grows with followers, not posts
Posts take longer to create from the user's perspective

defend.explain: The post is acknowledged immediately and fanned out asynchronously — the author never waits. The real costs are the celebrity tail, wasted work on dormant users, and storage that scales with the follow graph.

checkpoints.title: Capacity ladder
checkpoints.prompt: ~500M daily active users and ~100M posts per day.

rungs.q: Which operation is far more frequent
rungs.note: Hundreds of millions of sessions against 100M posts — reads dominate heavily.

rungs.q: Where media should be served from
rungs.note: Images and video are static and hot; they belong at the edge.

checkpoints.explain: Posting is a modest write rate. The scale problem is the fan-out multiplier and the media egress, not the post itself.

checkpoints.title: Architecture builder
checkpoints.explain: The timeline is a precomputed list of post ids in Redis; the post store hydrates them. Media comes from the CDN in a separate request the client makes directly. Fanout Workers and Kafka build timelines on the write path and never appear on a read.

checkpoints.title: Spot the bottleneck
checkpoints.prompt: Feeds load instantly but images take seconds to appear.
checkpoints.explain: The metadata path is healthy — ids arrive instantly. The CDN hit rate collapsed, so nearly every image is now a round trip to origin, and blob egress has risen to match. Usually this is a cache-key change: a new signed-URL parameter or resize token that varies per request makes every URL unique and therefore uncacheable.

wrong.Blob Storage: Elevated egress is the consequence of the misses, not the cause.
wrong.Redis timeline: 97% and unchanged — the feed itself is fine.
wrong.Feed Service: 45ms. It returned the post ids; fetching the media is a separate path.
